{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgFXSVV6QkwNRc96qacbf","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"=== BEGIN ARTIFACT ANALYSIS.md ===\n# Blueprint Analysis: LayersTesting\n\n## Commander Expectations\n\n- assert `sh sources/run.sh` exits zero against the completed ledger.\n- assert a rejected command exits with its documented code and changes nothing.\n- assert no command leaves an account balance below zero.\n- assert every report is computed from the database and matches the known answers.\n- assert all storage goes through the generated persistence layer selected by `DATABASE_URL`.\n\n## Crew\n\n| Crew | Charge |\n|---|---|\n| Commander | Defines intent and decides what done means. |\n| Team Lead | Confirms epic completeness and stakeholder expectations. |\n| Planning Crew | Authors atomic specifications and the ordered Manifest. |\n| Shipyard Crew | Builds the tickets without synchronous Commander access. |\n\n## Story List\n\n### Feature: Command Line Interface\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| CLI-001 | Ledger executable at the application root | `ledger` is an executable at the application root that dispatches every command. |\n| CLI-002 | Usage errors | Unknown command, table, or report, and wrong argument count exit 2 with empty stdout. |\n| CLI-003 | Help text for every command | `--help` lists every command, and each command and sub-verb has usage help text. |\n| CLI-004 | CSV success output and failure diagnostics | Successful commands write a header and comma-separated rows with `\\n` endings; failures write nothing to stdout and one stderr line. |\n| CLI-005 | Amount output format | Output amounts have exactly two decimals, a leading `-` when negative, and no thousands separator. |\n\n### Feature: Database Access\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| DB-001 | Database selection | `DATABASE_URL` selects the store; otherwise `DATABASE_PATH`, then `data/app.db`; `postgres://` and `postgresql://` select PostgreSQL. |\n| DB-002 | Generated persistence access | The three tables are reached only through the generated relational layer, and each write command commits in one database transaction. |\n| DB-003 | Integer-cent amount storage | Amounts are stored as integer cents and never as floating point. |\n| DB-004 | Operational failure | An unreachable database or missing table exits 1 with one stderr line. |\n\n### Feature: Schema Lifecycle\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| SCHEMA-001 | Initialize empty schema | `init` drops any present tables, creates the three tables empty, and writes nothing. |\n| SCHEMA-002 | Row counts | `count` writes `table,rows`, then the accounts, categories, and transactions rows. |\n\n### Feature: Input Validation\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| VAL-001 | Code validation | Account and category codes are 1 to 12 characters from `A-Z` and `0-9`. |\n| VAL-002 | Name, description, and memo validation | Names and descriptions are 1 to 40 characters, memos 0 to 60, and none contains a comma or newline. |\n| VAL-003 | Amount input validation | Amounts match `-?DIGITS[.D[D]]`, have at most two decimals, and are never zero. |\n| VAL-004 | Date validation | Dates are real calendar dates written `YYYY-MM-DD`. |\n| VAL-005 | Non-negative balance guard | Any command that would leave an account below zero exits 3 before its first write. |\n\n### Feature: Accounts\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| ACCT-001 | Add account | `account add` writes the new row with 0 transactions and balance 0.00; a duplicate code exits 3. |\n| ACCT-002 | Get account | `account get` writes the row; an absent code exits 4. |\n| ACCT-003 | Rename account | `account rename` writes the updated row; an absent code exits 4. |\n| ACCT-004 | Delete account | `account delete` writes `deleted` and the code; an account with through the generated relational layer, and each write command commits in one database transaction. |\n| DB-003 | Integer-cent amount storage | Amounts are stored as integer cents and never as floating point. |\n| DB-004 | Operational failure | An unreachable database or missing table exits 1 with one stderr line. |\n\n### Feature: Schema Lifecycle\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| SCHEMA-001 | Initialize empty schema | `init` drops any present tables, creates the three tables empty, and writes nothing. |\n| SCHEMA-002 | Row counts | `count` writes `table,rows`, then the accounts, categories, and transactions rows. |\n\n### Feature: Input Validation\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| VAL-001 | Code validation | Account and category codes are 1 to 12 characters from `A-Z` and `0-9`. |\n| VAL-002 | Name, description, and memo validation | Names and descriptions are 1 to 40 characters, memos 0 to 60, and none contains a comma or newline. |\n| VAL-003 | Amount input validation | Amounts match `-?DIGITS[.D[D]]`, have at most two decimals, and are never zero. |\n| VAL-004 | Date validation | Dates are real calendar dates written `YYYY-MM-DD`. |\n| VAL-005 | Non-negative balance guard | Any command that would leave an account below zero exits 3 before its first write. |\n\n### Feature: Accounts\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| ACCT-001 | Add account | `account add` writes the new row with 0 transactions and balance 0.00; a duplicate code exits 3. |\n| ACCT-002 | Get account | `account get` writes the row; an absent code exits 4. |\n| ACCT-003 | Rename account | `account rename` writes the updated row; an absent code exits 4. |\n| ACCT-004 | Delete account | `account delete` writes `deleted` and the code; an account with transactions exits 3; an absent code exits 4. |\n\n### Feature: Bulk Load\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| LOAD-001 | Load accounts | `load accounts` checks the header, validates every row, rejects duplicate keys, and stores all rows or none. |\n| LOAD-002 | Load categories | `load categories` follows the same all-or-nothing contract for and header check | An unreadable file exits 1; a header that does not match the table's columns exits 3. |\n\n### Feature: Transactions\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| TXN-001 | Post transaction | `txn post` assigns the next id, validates account, category, amount, date, and memo, and writes the row. |\n| TXN-002 | Get transaction | `txn get` writes the row; an absent id exits 4. |\n| TXN-003 | Amend transaction | `txn amend` changes only the amount, applies the balance guard, and exits 4 when the id is absent. |\n| TXN-004 | Delete transaction | `txn delete` writes `deleted` and the id, applies the balance guard, and exits 4 when the id is absent. |\n\n### Feature: Transfers\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| XFER-001 | Transfer | `transfer` writes two TRANSFER rows with consecutive ids, or writes nothing when rejected. |\n\n### Feature: Reports\n\n| ID | Story | High-level AC |\n|---|---|---|\n| RPT-001 | Balances report | `report balances` lists accounts by code with counts and balances, then a TOTAL row. |\n| RPT-002 | Categories report | `report categories` lists every category by code, including unused ones, with inflow, outflow, net, and a TOTAL row. |\n| RPT-003 | Monthly report | `report monthly` lists each month that has transactions in ascending order, then a TOTAL row. |\n\n### Feature: Automated Tests\n\n| ID | context | stage |\n\n## Planning Instructions\n\n### Delivery Shape\n\nThe product is a single-process Python command-line program, the `ledger` executable at the application root, invoked once per command. Inputs are argv and CSV files named by `load`. State lives in a relational store: SQLite by default, PostgreSQL when `DATABASE_URL` is a PostgreSQL DSN. Outputs are CSV on stdout, one diagnostic line on stderr for failures, and an exit code from 0 to 4. Each command validates all inputs and the balance guard, then performs its writes in one database transaction. The supplied `sh sources/run.sh` drives acceptance from the application root.\n\n### Story Realization Map\n\n| Story | Durable scope | Evidence | Kind |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| CLI-001 | `ledger` entry point at the application root | `sources/INSTRUCTIONS.md` Objective;
